- Neovim is selected through the first shorthand backend, `vfox:mise-plugins/vfox-neovim`; that plugin treats every non-`arm64` Linux architecture as x86_64.
- Pixi uses `github:prefix-dev/pixi`; its ARM32 release has no binary, and mise’s generic matcher accepts the platform-neutral `source.tar.gz`.
- The remaining tools use Aqua, where mise changes Rust `arm` to `armv6l`, bypassing Aqua registry replacements keyed on Go’s canonical `arm`.

I’m checking the exact fix boundaries and whether current tests cover these safety properties before wrapping up.

content.text:
The report is valid, but it combines three separate defects—not one Aqua bug.

1. Neovim: vfox plugin bug

The shorthand prefers vfox before Aqua in [registry/neovim.toml](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/a816/mise/registry/neovim.toml:1). Mise passes `arm` correctly to vfox, but [vfox-neovim’s installer](https://github.com/mise-plugins/vfox-neovim/blob/main/hooks/pre_install.lua) handles only `arm64`; every other Linux architecture falls into the x86_64 branch.

Neovim 0.12.5 publishes only x86_64 and ARM64 Linux builds, so ARM32 should fail as unsupported. This needs a separate vfox-neovim fix that rejects unknown architectures.

2. Pixi: unsafe GitHub asset fallback

Pixi uses the GitHub backend, not Aqua, as shown in [registry/pixi.toml](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/a816/mise/registry/pixi.toml:1).

Pixi 0.80.0 has no ARM32 binary. Mise correctly rejects explicitly wrong-architecture assets, but the generic matcher gives archives a positive score and does not exclude names such as `source.tar.gz`; see [asset_matcher.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/a816/mise/src/backend/asset_matcher.rs:345). Consequently, the source archive becomes the only ostensibly compatible candidate.

The GitHub matcher should reject recognizable source-only archives during automatic selection, while still allowing an explicit `asset_pattern` for projects that intentionally install one.

3. Aqua tools: incorrect ARM32 identity and incomplete metadata

The direct cause of the repeated `armv6l` names is [aqua.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/a816/mise/src/backend/aqua.rs:5229):

```rust
cfg!(target_arch = "arm") => "armv6l"
```

Aqua itself uses Go architecture names, where 32-bit ARM is `arm`, not `armv6l`; its [runtime implementation](https://github.com/aquaproj/aqua/blob/main/pkg/runtime/runtime.go) passes `runtime.GOARCH` through unchanged.

Mise is also internally inconsistent: target-platform resolution already passes `arm` through unchanged in [aqua.rs](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/a816/mise/src/backend/aqua.rs:1106), while current-host URL generation changes it to `armv6l`.

Changing that mapping to canonical `arm` is necessary, but not sufficient for every listed tool. Aqua metadata must then map `arm` to each project’s actual spelling—`arm`, `armv7`, `armhf`, or an `eabihf` target. Aqua currently treats ARM32 as only partially supported, so several registry entries will need upstream metadata changes.

Recommended fix split:

- mise PR: canonicalize Aqua ARM32 as `arm`, reject automatic source-archive selection, and add ARM32 regression tests.
- vfox-neovim PR: error on unsupported architectures instead of defaulting to x86_64.
- Aqua registry PR(s): add explicit ARM32 replacements/overrides for packages that genuinely publish compatible artifacts.
- Optional completeness: allow `linux-arm` in cross-platform lock validation; [Platform::validate](/Users/jdx/.codex/worktrees/a816/mise/src/platform.rs:75) currently excludes it.

No files were changed. [Discussion #12996](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/12996) currently has no replies.
